title: Progressive disclosure: compact index (knowledge_index + link traversal) -> drill into articles
priority_note: The 'load the index, then drill' half — reduces over-retrieval. Built on knowledge_index + article_link (NOT the OKF full-export Markdown, which is not topic-scoped). Depends on the curated rule (31.1).

background.reference: GitHub issues #305/#306 ('OKF index files for progressive disclosure'); hub 820602df. Review round 1: okf.ex's index.md is a PRIVATE, full-tenant, project-scoped Markdown export (render_category_index/render_root_index are defp) — NOT a topic-scoped stub source; and hubs are emergent (article_link degree), not a modeled type.
background.includes: Rather than over-retrieving chunks, an agent loads a compact, capped index of relevant curated-source stubs and drills into only the chosen ones. Built from knowledge_index (id/title/category) + article_link traversal + okf.ex derive_description/1 for the one-line summary — not a new index store, and not the OKF full export.

story.i_want_to: fetch a compact, capped index of relevant curated-source stubs for a topic and then drill into only the chosen articles
story.so_that: I navigate by index in a bounded number of tokens instead of over-retrieving many fuzzy chunks

rationale: Karpathy's 'navigate by index' and the OKF index-file pattern both say read a compact index and follow the few relevant pages. loopctl already has knowledge_index + links + a description helper; composing them into a bounded, topic-scoped stub query is the token-efficiency half of the hybrid interface — without over-claiming a capability okf.ex's full-export index does not have.

acceptance_criteria.description: A progressive-disclosure entrypoint returns, for a topic/query, a COMPACT, CAPPED set of stubs (id, title, category, one-line summary via okf.ex derive_description/1 extracted to a shared/public helper) built from knowledge_index + article_link traversal — NOT full bodies, and NOT the OKF full-export Markdown. Tenant-scoped.
The index is bounded: a configurable top-K cap on stubs (and traversal fan-out) so a densely-linked hub does not flood context; the cap is documented and tested.
A drill step fetches the full body of a chosen indexed article by id (scope-enforced), so the agent loads only what the index pointed at.

The index prefers governed curated sources (US-31.1) and, if hub enrichment is used, defines a hub operationally as an article with >= N outgoing :relates_to article_links (hubs are not a modeled type). Tenant isolation: index + drill only expose the caller tenant's articles (system-scope per US-31.1 AC-31.1.3).

test_cases.name: index returns capped compact stubs then drill returns the body
preconditions: an article with > top-K outgoing :relates_to links to curated articles (an operational hub)
steps: fetch the progressive index for the topic
expected_results: index returns <= top-K stubs (id/title/category/summary, not full bodies); drill returns the full body; token-compact and capped

technical_notes: Build on the knowledge_index controller/context (id/title/category, index.js ~2443) + article_link :relates_to traversal + okf.ex derive_description/1 (make it public/shared for the one-liner).

okf.ex index.md (render_category_index/render_root_index, defp) is a FULL-tenant, project-scoped Markdown export bounded by max_buffered_export_articles — it is NOT a topic-scoped stub source; do not reuse it for this query.
Hub is emergent (>= N outgoing :relates_to links via article_link), not a field/category/tag.
Cap traversal fan-out (the code already bounds high-degree hub fan-out elsewhere — mirror it).
Tenant scoping is explicit-predicate on AdminRepo/HeavyRead.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2 with explicit article_link rows (not a nonexistent hub type).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (review, US-31.3): the seed step actually implemented is search_keyword/3 (a websearch_to_tsquery full-text matcher), NOT the knowledge_index controller/context named above -- knowledge_index is a category/tag CATALOG browse with no topic scoping, so it cannot satisfy AC-31.3.1's 'for a topic/query' requirement as-is. search_keyword/3 was substituted deliberately as the topic-scoped seed; article_link :relates_to traversal (this story's other named building block) is implemented as designed. Caveat: a fuzzy tsquery can silently omit a curated article that is topically relevant but shares no lexical tokens with the query and is not linked from a lexically-matching hub -- the hub traversal partially mitigates by recovering linked-but-lexically-disjoint neighbors, but does not fully close the gap. Documented here explicitly per review finding rather than left as a silent building-block swap.
